content:
Do yourself a favor and get yourself some good tools for this project. While you can get your work done with these tools, having the right tools will speed up the process and really limit your frustration. Some tools that I used were:

* Flush cutters (good for removing rivets too).
* T-handle metric socket set with ball end. I used Park Tool set, but any T-handle will do.
* Electronics driver kit. I used iFixit Mako Driver kit with 64 bits. It comes with a flexible extension that was REALLY useful for tight spaces.
* Electric screwdriver kit.
* ESD tweezers kit. Preferably one with a round tip.
* Head lamp
* A 5.5mm 6-point socket or a tiny flat plier to hold the M3 nuts.
* M3 tap
* An INDX-specific 3D-printed hardware bin.
* Nitrile gloves
* Prusa grease and linear motor grease kit (it's a good time to do some maintenance while you're at it).
* Tape measure
* Blue shop towels

The header of this section reads "All the required tools are included."  However the opposite is true:  NONE of the required tools are included with this INDX conversion kit.  Further down users are directed to use the tools originally included with the CORE One+ / CORE One Printer.

replies.content: +1 to this. Had a lot of fun unscrewing things with a needle nose because they couldn't include a new 10 cent wrench :/
